items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: I'm thinking of Hormann particularly but the other men too.

ctx.x: like that, huh? And a clarinet man is the same thing, exactly the same way. Our first clarinet man, Dick Ramberg, he had a lot of trouble with that so I kept after him to shake because I'd seen Raymond do that and I'd seen George too. And you know, it's not vibrato all the time. Kid Thomas plays, well, no, he puts, the vibrato is usually at the end of a phrase. It holds a note and shakes it. Yeah, you hold a note and at the end you shake it, you know. But you can have it going in the middle part too but it's most…
Well, how do they crack it? Now, explain that again. In the middle of a phrase?
